tip: Disable the optimization that removes unused native types from dart:html and related libraries.

tip: Disable type inference.

option.name: --dump-info=
tip: Generates information about the generated code.
'format' can be either 'json' or 'binary'.
You can inspect the generated data using tools from 'package:dart2js_info'.

option.name: --enable-asserts
tip: Enable assertions.

tip: Add colors to diagnostic messages.

option.name: --fatal-warnings
tip: Treat warnings as compilation errors.

option.name: --generate-code-with-compile-time-errors
tip: Generates output even if the program contains compile-time errors.
Use the exit code to determine if compilation failed.

option.name: --help
tip: Print this usage information (add -v for information about all options).

option.name: --lax-runtime-type-to-string
tip: Omits reified class type arguments when these are only needed for `toString` on `runtimeType`.
This is useful if `runtimeType.toString()` is only used for debugging.
Note that semantics of other uses of `.runtimeType`, for instance `a.runtimeType == b.runtimeType`, is not affected by this flag.

option.name: --libraries-spec=
tip: A .json file containing the SDK libraries specification.

option.name: --minify
tip: Generate minified output.

option.name: --native-null-assertions
tip: Add assertions to web library APIs to ensure that non-nullable APIs do not return null.
This is set to true by default unless -O3 or higher is passed.

option.name: --no-frequency-based-minification
tip: Experimental.
Disable the new frequency based minifying namer and use the old namer instead.

option.name: --no-source-maps
tip: Do not generate a source map file.

option.name: --omit-implicit-checks
tip: Omit implicit runtime checks, such as parameter checks and implicit downcasts.
These checks are included by default in Dart 2.0.
By using this flag the checks are removed, however the compiler will assume that all such checks were valid and may use this information for optimizations.
Use this option only if you have enough testing to ensure that your program works with the checks.

option.name: --omit-late-names
tip: Do not include names of late variables in error messages.
This allows the compiler to generate smaller code by removing late variable names from the generated JavaScript.

This can be an absolute or relative path.

option.name: --server-mode
tip: Compile with server support.
The compiler will use a library specification that disables dart:html but supports dart:js in conditional imports.

option.name: --show-package-warnings
tip: Show warnings and hints generated from packages.

option.name: --suppress-hints
tip: Do not display any hints.

option.name: --suppress-warnings
tip: Do not display any warnings.

option.name: --terse
tip: Emit diagnostics without suggestions for how to get rid of the diagnosed problems.

option.name: --throw-on-error
tip: Throw an exception if a compile-time error is detected.

option.name: --trust-primitives
tip: Assume that operations on numbers, strings, and lists have valid inputs.
This option allows the compiler to drop runtime checks for those operations.
Note: a well-typed program is not guaranteed to have valid inputs.
For example, an int index argument may be null or out of range.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Display verbose information.

option.name: --version
tip: Display version information.

option.name: -O
tip: Set the compiler optimization level (defaults to -O1).
No optimizations (only meant for debugging the compiler).
Default (includes whole program analyses and inlining).
Safe production-oriented optimizations (like minification).
Potentially unsafe optimizations (see -h -v for details).
More aggressive unsafe optimizations (see -h -v for details).
